**Goal:** publish a working, privacy-safe technical portfolio quickly. The website can be simple. The important skill is versioning, testing and publishing your own work.

## Repository and website

Use the school-approved GitHub identity. Do not post personal contact information, student photographs without consent or private school network information.

Create a new public repository, for example `tej-portfolio`, with a README. Clone it to your own computer and add a minimal `index.html`:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1">
  <title>Computer Engineering Portfolio</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Computer Engineering Portfolio</h1>
  <p>Projects, experiments, tests and what I learned.</p>
  <h2>Projects</h2>
  <ul><li><a href="linux.html">Linux computer setup</a></li></ul>
</body>
</html>
```

Create `linux.html` (or remove the unfinished link) before submitting. Record what you worked on without naming classmates or publishing machine passwords.

## Version-control essentials

From inside the clone:

```bash
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Publish first portfolio page"
git push
```

Use `git log --oneline` to inspect history. Learn the difference between a repository on your computer and GitHub's remote copy.

## GitHub Pages

In the repository Settings > Pages, select the approved deployment source and branch/folder used by your site. Save and open the published URL. The URL pattern depends on whether you used a user site or project site, so **copy the actual URL from GitHub rather than guessing**.

Check the site on another device. Verify working links, readable layout and mobile width. Record the repository URL and published URL.

Official reference: [GitHub Pages quickstart](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/quickstart).

## Keep updating it

Each major project gets a small post: **Goal -> Tools/commands -> Tests -> Results -> Problems solved -> What I learned**. Commit the update. Next useful lesson: [technical blog reporting](09-technical-blog.qmd).
